claim: The author announced Datasette Agent 0.5a0 on November 3, 2026 and Datasette Apps 0.3a0 on November 4, 2026.
passages: Posted 3rd November 2026 at 11:13 pm
Posted 4th November 2026 at 12:29 am
locator: Each author post: RELEASE heading and Posted line
qualifiers: Dates are author publication dates, not inferred from GitHub timestamps.
limitations: Captured release pages did not render a release timestamp; local post times have no timezone stated in the capture.

claim: Agent 0.5a0 adds a Datasette-page panel and permission-checked table, database and stored-query references; conversations pin their selected model.
passages: New panel next to the chat that shows Datasette pages.
Permission checks run as the user sending the message.
The model is pinned for the life of that conversation
locator: 0.5a0 release notes: model chooser, # references and panel bullets
qualifiers: Event date is associated with the dated author announcement.
limitations: Documentation observation only; no UI interaction or framing compatibility test.

claim: Apps 0.3a0 adds app references, query-grant tools, creation-time query visibility/existence checks and approval for write-query grants; app links open in the Agent panel and tool results include relative paths.
passages: Granting a write query requires approval from the user first.
app_create() now checks that each requested stored query exists and that the user can view it
App tool results now include the app's relative path
locator: 0.3a0 release notes: integration bullets; author release post
limitations: These access and approval mechanisms do not establish generated SQL correctness; no working integration was tested.

claim: Agent 0.5a0 Stop keeps streamed text, allows an already-started tool to finish and stops before the next step; conversations continue after navigation.
passages: A tool that has already started is allowed to finish
Conversations keep running if you navigate away.
locator: 0.5a0 release notes: Stop button and continuing-conversation bullets
qualifiers: Not an assertion of rollback or cancellation of an in-flight write.

claim: As documented on November 8, execute_write_sql analyzes ordered statements before explicit approval, executes with actor permissions, and retains earlier successes if a later statement fails; saving queries requires approval.
passages: asks the user for explicit approval in chat before anything runs.
later statements are skipped and earlier successes are not rolled back.
Saving always requires human approval
locator: Current README: Executing write SQL; Saving queries
qualifiers: Current main-branch README observation on November 8, not exclusively attributed to 0.5a0.
limitations: No runtime or transaction-behavior test; permissions and approval do not certify query intent.

claim: Agent 0.5a0 requires Python 3.11+, Datasette 1.0a41+, datasette-llm 0.1a9+ and llm 0.37.1+; Apps 0.3a0 requires Datasette 1.0a41+ and drops Python 3.10.
passages: Minimum versions are now datasette>=1.0a41, datasette-llm>=0.1a9 and llm>=0.37.1.
Now requires Python 3.11 or later
Now requires Datasette 1.0a41 or higher.
dropped support for Python 3.10.
locator: Dependency and Python bullets at end of tagged release notes
qualifiers: Documented minima, not a certified tested environment.
limitations: Package installation and cross-version compatibility were not tested.

claim: The current README installs Agent into the Datasette environment and describes model availability as API-key availability filtered by configured allowlists/blocklists and tool-calling support.
passages: Install this plugin in the same environment as Datasette.
models whose API key is available
minus any that cannot call tools
locator: Current README: Installation; Choosing a model
qualifiers: Observed November 8, 2026; provider model examples were not treated as an independently verified availability list.
limitations: No provider sign-in, API call, billing or model-capability test.

claim: datasette-llm 0.1a10 fixes overriding previously configured model allowlists; the author reported that model restrictions on his demo had been affected.
passages: Fixed a bug where this plugin over-rode previously configured allow-lists of models.
Fixes a bug that affected my agent.datasette.io demo site
qualifiers: Author-reported bug and fix; the patch is newer than Agent 0.5a0 minimum datasette-llm 0.1a9.
limitations: No reproduction or verification that the combined installation enforces the intended model set.

claim: The current Apps README distinguishes sandboxed managed HTML/JavaScript apps from unrestricted Python plugin apps; managed apps require configured HTTPS origins for direct network access.
passages: Stored apps are rendered inside a sandboxed iframe.
Apps provided by other plugins that are written in Python and HTML/JavaScript which are unrestricted
Direct network access is blocked unless the app has exact https:// origins configured.
locator: Current README: Usage; Sandboxed apps; External apps from plugins
qualifiers: Observed current README on November 8, 2026; sandbox claims apply to managed HTML apps only.
limitations: No isolation audit; explicitly allowed origins can receive app requests.

claim: Managed app data requests use app-scoped endpoints and app allowlists while preserving current-actor Datasette permissions; failed queries and JavaScript/resource failures are exposed in the error panel.
passages: the parent page forwards them to an app-scoped query endpoint.
Datasette's normal SQL and query permissions still apply.
Failed stored-query attempts
locator: Current README: Data access; Sandboxed apps
qualifiers: Current documentation observed November 8; grants do not establish result correctness.
limitations: No query, error-display or access-control test.

claim: Current app tags expose identifier, URL and editability; reading HTML source separately with app_view requires edit-app permission.
passages: The agent is told the tagged app's ID and URL and whether you can edit it.
app_view tool, which requires edit-app permission.
locator: Current README: Tagging apps in datasette-agent
limitations: No source-access permission test was performed.

claim: The actual current LICENSE files for Agent and Apps contain the Apache License, Version 2.0.
passages: Apache License
Version 2.0, January 2004
locator: Both inspected LICENSE files: opening title and full terms
qualifiers: Current main-branch code licenses observed November 8, 2026.
limitations: This does not establish dataset, provider-service or generated-output rights; tagged-version license history was not separately compared.

claim: All three inspected version pages mark their releases as prereleases.
passages: 0.5a0 Pre-release
0.3a0 Pre-release
0.1a10 Pre-release
qualifiers: Release status is not an independent reliability measurement.
